item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在South African Institute of International Affairs (SAIIA)--South Africa官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
2nd Africa Annual Conference on Credit Ratings Towards Developing African Capital Markets

发布源: South African Institute of International Affairs (SAIIA)--South Africa | 抓取时间: 2026-10-26

Africa today faces a defining paradox: the continent is widely perceived as capital-scarce and highly risky, yet it holds significant domestic financial resources that could help finance its transformation.

Against this backdrop, the African Peer Review Mechanism, the UN Economic Commission for Africa, UN Development Programme, AfriCatalyst, SAIIA and other strategic partners are convening the 2ndAfrica Annual Conference on Credit Ratings.

Under the theme “Towards Developing African Capital Markets: Rechannelling Africa’s Capital,” the conference advanced actionable reforms to help African capital remain, circulate, and grow within the continent in support of sustainable development, industrialisation, regional integration, and economic resilience.

Bringing together policymakers, central bankers, regulators, institutional investors, credit rating agencies, development finance institutions, academics, and market participants, the conference explored ways to reform credit rating systems, mobilise domestic capital, deepen African financial markets, reduce borrowing costs, and strengthen Africa’s financial sovereignty.

Strategic pillar 4

A system that tracks our results, holds us to account and helps us improve.

Monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning, often shortened to MEAL, helps FANRPAN deliver on its mandate with transparency, efficiency and measurable results.

We are building one system for tracking progress, capturing lessons and improving every programme and thematic area. Data are collected in the same way across projects, countries learn from one another, and programmes change course when the evidence says they should.

This makes us more accountable to the governments, partners and communities we work with. It also makes our own decisions better informed.

Define the indicators and measures that track performance and outcomes.

Use standard systems so that results are measured the same way in every project.

Support national data systems that serve the goals of agrifood systems transformation.

Use evaluation findings to refine strategies and make programmes work better.

The MEAL framework will not only enhance accountability but also strengthen evidence-informed decision-making.

Strategic pillar 2

Better access to evidence that supports agrifood systems policy transformation.

Knowledge and advocacy

Policy has long been shaped mostly by the state, with little input from other actors.

FANRPAN works to give researchers, farmer organisations, agribusiness, parliamentarians and the media a stronger voice in agricultural and food policy debates. We turn complex evidence into products people can use, and bring stakeholders together in dialogue.

We also help countries and stakeholders understand continental frameworks, such as the African Continental Free Trade Area, the African Union climate change strategy and biodiversity frameworks.

IRR welcomes crypto rethink, calls for exchange controls to be scrappedOct 22, 2026

发布源: South African Institute of Race Relations (IRR) --South Africa | 抓取时间: 2026-10-26

The Institute of Race Relations (IRR) welcomes the decision by National Treasury and the South African Reserve Bank to rewrite their draft rules on moving crypto assets across South Africa’s borders.

In his Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement, the finance minister, Enoch Godongwana, told Parliament that the thousands of comments received showed the need for “a different approach”, and that a revised draft would be released for public comment.

The IRR was among those who made detailed submissions. In itsSubmission to the National Treasury regarding the Draft Capital Flow Management Regulations, it argued that the regulations were unconstitutional, economically unwise and should be withdrawn. In itsSubmission to the South African Reserve Bank regarding the draft Crypto-Asset Manual for cross-border activities, it recommended that the manual be withdrawn and exchange controls repealed.

“The sheer volume of comment shows how much South Africans care about this,” says IRR CEO John Endres. “Treasury and the Reserve Bank were right to listen.”

“Whatever rules emerge now should make it easier for South Africans to use these new technologies, not harder. Payment systems around the world are being digitised and tokenised at speed. South Africa should embrace that shift, not watch the opportunities pass it by.”

Endres says the drafts should be judged against the state of the economy.

item.title: [South African Institute of Race Relations (IRR) --South Africa] The Hoernlé Memorial Lectures
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在South African Institute of Race Relations (IRR) --South Africa官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
The Hoernlé Memorial Lectures

发布源: South African Institute of Race Relations (IRR) --South Africa | 抓取时间: 2026-10-26

The inaugural Hoernlé lecture was delivered by Jan Hendrik Hofmeyr, IRR vice-president and honorary life member, in 1945 on the topic of “Christian principles and race problems”. Other distinguished speakers included IRR co-founder Professor Edgar Brookes on the Institute’s first 21 years in “We come of age” (1950), Archbishop Dennis Hurley on “Apartheid: A crisis of the Christian conscience” (1964), Chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi on “White and black nationalism, ethnicity and the future of the homelands” (1974), Dr Alan Paton on “Towards racial justice: Will there be a change of heart?” (1979) and again on “Federation or desolation” (1985) – the only speaker to have delivered two Hoernlé lectures – Professor Jonathan Jansen on “When does a university cease to exist?” (2005) and Professor RW Johnson on “The future of the liberal tradition in South Africa” (2011).

The speakers often tackled thorny questions relating to race, ideology and South Africa’s future. In their explorations, they reflected the most pressing preoccupations of their times, giving us a window into the past that shows contemporary views on issues that often seemed intractable at the time. It is sobering to look back from today’s vantage point and realise how far South Africa has come – and how much still remains to be done to create a free and prosperous South Africa for all.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在South African Institute of Race Relations (IRR) --South Africa官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
History of the IRR Bursary Programme (1936-2022)

发布源: South African Institute of Race Relations (IRR) --South Africa | 抓取时间: 2026-10-26

From a time of simple racial segregation in the first part of the twentieth century, through the intensified racial regime of the apartheid period and for nearly three decades into post-apartheid democracy, about 6,000 black South Africans graduated from universities, technikons and other tertiary institutions thanks to the bursary programme administered by the South African Institute of Race Relations (SAIRR). Immense hurdles had to be overcome, both by the students themselves as well as funders and administrators.

While unquestionably delivering positive outcomes, the programme was often caught up in the turbulence of the times, especially during the popular resistance from the mid-1970s to the early 1990s. If not itself the subject of controversy, it was often linked to controversy and conflict around matters like reform versus revolution, disinvestment versus business influence, and armed struggle versus peaceful resistance. This is the story of that bursary programme and the tumultuous times in which it operated.

The South African Institute of Race Relations (SAIRR) is a classically liberal not-for-profit organisation, founded in 1929 with the objective of improving relations between South Africa's race groups. This almost immediately became a matter of opposing racial discrimination and promoting the establishment of a non-racial society in South Africa. item.content:encoded:
Economic Integration Program

发布源: Mandela Institute for Development Studies (MINDS) --South Africa | 抓取时间: 2026-10-26

REGIONAL COOPERATION

Accelerating Africa’s growth requires stronger cross-sector partnerships and deeper regional integration.

PROGRAM RESPONSE

Through the Economic Integration Program, MINDS underscores the urgency of advancing integration as a driver of Africa’s development. Despite strong continental intent, fragmented markets persist, limiting growth. The program promotes practical implementation, strengthens regional value chains, and improves market access to support the shift from policy ambition to meaningful, sustained economic transformation.

APPLYING KNOWLEDGE

Through inclusive, multi-sectoral dialogues, the MINDS High-Level Dialogue Series strengthens relationships across Africa, helping leaders from all sectors create shared visions and work together to tackle the continent’s complex development issues.

item.content:encoded:
African Heritage Program

发布源: Mandela Institute for Development Studies (MINDS) --South Africa | 抓取时间: 2026-10-26

CULTURE AND DEVELOPMENT

The African Heritage Program explores African people, culture and heritage to ground development in Africanness. Through rigorous research, it deepens the understanding of African identity and value systems to inform development practice.

FOUNDATIONAL APPROACH

MINDS believes that a better understanding of Africanness begins with systematic research and rigorous analysis of African heritage. This work seeks to develop an inclusive conceptualisation of Africanness, grounded in the values,and lived realities of African societies. Anchored in this understanding, the programme aims to inform development initiatives that are culturally grounded and more effective in addressing Africa’s development challenges.

APPLYING KNOWLEDGE

The Program identifies foundational African principles across governance, leadership and knowledge domains, applying these insights to assess and shape development initiatives.
